back: Land acquired only from owners who chose to sell, at a fair price (Lancaster House, 1980-1990).

front: When did the Fast Track Land Reform Programme begin?

back: A1: smallholder family plots; A2: medium and large commercial farms (fast-track reform).

front: What did the Land Acquisition Act (1992) allow?
back: Compulsory acquisition of land with compensation.

front: What does the 2013 Constitution say about compensation for acquired land?
back: Compensation is paid for improvements (buildings, dams), not for the land itself.
Increasing indigenous Zimbabwean ownership of the economy; the 2007 Act required 51% indigenous ownership of larger businesses.

front: How did Western countries react to fast-track land reform?
back: Criticism; EU measures from 2002; US act of 2001; Commonwealth suspension (2002). The government called them illegal sanctions.

front: Give two benefits and two problems of land reform.
back: Benefits: land for many families, wider ownership. Problems: fall in output and exports, farm workers displaced (also lack of title and credit).

front: Name two gender-equity measures in the 2013 Constitution.
back: 60 reserved National Assembly seats for women; the Zimbabwe Gender Commission (and equal access to land).
